valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E. At the 12-month target date (Nov 2027) an investor prices next-twelve-month EPS, about 3/4 FY2028 (Aug-2028 year end) plus 1/4 FY2029. Base: FY2026 reported diluted EPS $20.76 (includes a $0.15 Q4 tariff-refund benefit); FY2027 $23.10 (about +11%, in line with published estimates of $22.70-23.25), FY2028 $25.80, FY2029 $28.70; blended NTM about $26.50. Model assumptions, not guidance. The $30 special dividend (ex-date 2026-11-24) is excluded from targets: they are ex-special prices, and the dividend is shown separately. USD listing, no ADR conversion.

bear.driver: Comparable sales fade toward 4-5%, tariff-refund and gasoline tailwinds reverse, membership fee/renewal momentum slows, EPS growth about 5% a year; multiple compresses toward the long-run premium-staples range

base.driver: Net sales growth about 8-9% from 33 FY27 openings and comps, steady gross margin, SG&A leverage, fee income compounding; EPS growth about 11-12%

bull.driver: Comps stay near 6-7% ex-gas, digital and membership growth accelerate, operating margin expands; EPS growth about 14-15%

valuation.implied_by_close: At base NTM EPS $26.50 the $1,106.21 close implies 41.7x; the base 40x gives $1,060. The latest named targets are $1,150-1,155 (JPMorgan, Bernstein), which need 43.4-43.6x at $26.50 or about $28.8-28.9 EPS at 40x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $26.50 (2.4 pp of return on the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Ex-gas, ex-FX comparable sales growth (6.7% in Q4 FY26) and membership fee income/renewal rate; ex-gas comps below about 5% would break the base case.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q1 FY2027 earnings (quarter ending about 2026-11-22), expected in mid-December 2026; monthly sales reports for November on about 2026-12-03.

analyst_notes: Seven named analysts found. After the Sep 24 Q4 report (EPS $6.75 vs $6.54 expected) Truist cut $1,011 to $955 and Roth held Sell at $781; since then JPMorgan raised $1,015 to $1,150 (Nov 5), Bernstein $1,143 to $1,155 (Nov 11) and Tigress $1,065 to $1,250 (Oct 15), while Freedom Broker moved to Hold on valuation. Bullish targets of $1,150-1,250 need about 43-47x on the $26.50 base EPS versus the 40x base; the targets are not stated ex the $30 special dividend. Horizons are unverified so no target enters the weighted figure; the sample is small and Mizuho (Nov 17) and Stifel (Nov 17) calls post-date the close and are excluded.
